The International Energy Agency (IEA) warns that oil stocks are being depleted at record rates, with prices remaining below historical highs but poised for significant increases if the strait of Hormuz remains closed.  Several analysts predict a "forced" adjustment to energy demand as prices rise, potentially leading to economic disruption and shortages. **The US** is facing increased costs for consumers due to rising global energy prices, while the **Institute for International Finance (IIF)** warns that the ripple effects of the disruption are spreading beyond oil markets, impacting other commodities like LNG and fertilizers.

recent_articles.title: UK teen rape victim says judge’s ruling felt ‘like a rock in my face’ after three boys spared jail | World News - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A **teenage rape victim** in Hampshire, UK, criticized the court's decision to hand three boys Youth Rehabilitation Orders instead of prison sentences for their assaults. The 16-year-old stated that she felt "like a rock straight in my face" after the ruling and questioned why she endured the trauma of reliving the assault during the trial. Her family also expressed disappointment with the sentencing outcome, calling it inadequate and urging authorities to reconsider the case.

recent_articles.title: Security forces kill 11 terrorists in KP's North Waziristan: ISPR - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Security forces** in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's North Waziristan district have killed **11 terrorists**, identified as members of the banned **Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan** (**Fitna-al-Khawarij**) during a series of intelligence-based operations over the past 48 hours.  Weapons and ammunition were recovered from the slain individuals, who were actively involved in numerous terrorist activities. The **ISPR** stated that sanitisation operations continue to eliminate remaining terrorists, as Pakistan's counter-terrorism campaign continues with full force to eradicate foreign-sponsored terrorism within the country.

recent_articles.title: Clashes in Belgrade as student-led protests demand elections | Police News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Students** and antigovernment protesters clashed with **riot police** in Belgrade on Saturday, demanding early elections and the rule of law. The demonstrations followed an anti-government rally organized by a youth movement that has challenged President **Aleksandar Vucic’s** hardline rule for over a year.  The protests were sparked by a train station tragedy in November 2024, which led to calls for accountability and corruption investigations.  **Vucic**, who was on a state visit to China, criticized the protesters' "violent nature" and vowed that Serbia would continue functioning within the law. The **Council of Europe’s** commissioner for human rights, Michael O’Flaherty, has expressed concern over the deterioration of Serbia's human rights situation and reported instances of police protecting attackers against journalists and protesters.

recent_articles.title: BBC at the site of China's worst mining disaster in more than a decade
recent_articles.rephrased_article: At least 82 people have been killed and two are missing after a gas explosion at the Liushenyu Coal Mine in Shanxi province, China.  **Chinese President Xi Jinping** has ordered full efforts for rescue operations. The blast is the worst mining disaster in China since 2009, according to state media reports. **The BBC's China correspondent Stephen McDonell** is at the scene of the blast.

recent_articles.title: Iran’s leader and security council ‘still need to approve’ peace deal with US | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Donald Trump** claimed a peace deal with **Iran** has been largely negotiated, but Iranian officials stated that one or two clauses need clarification before the memorandum of understanding can be sent to Iran's supreme national security council and supreme leader. The proposed deal reportedly offers sanctions relief in exchange for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and negotiating on its nuclear program over the next 60 days starting June 5th in Pakistan.  **Iran’s president Masoud Pezeshkian** expressed jubilant mood, while **US Secretary of State Marco Rubio** stated that the deal aims to address Iran's nuclear ambitions and open the Strait of Hormuz. Republican hawks criticized the proposed agreement as too lenient towards **Iran**, with former **CIA Director Mike Pompeo** calling it a "playbook" for building a WMD program.

recent_articles.title: Civilians must not be attacked ‘anywhere’, Pakistan tells UNSC - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Pakistan's** ambassador to the UN, Asim Iftikhar Ahmad, urged an immediate ceasefire and renewed diplomatic efforts to end the war in Ukraine during a UN Security Council emergency meeting.  He emphasized that civilians must not be attacked in armed conflict and called for lasting peace through dialogue and cessation of hostilities. **Unicef** director of operations and advocacy, Edem Wosornu, stated that nearly 16,000 civilians have been killed and over 44,000 injured in Ukraine since the war began in February 2022, while **Ted Chaiban**, deputy executive director of **Unicef**, highlighted that more than 3,400 children have been killed or injured since the escalation of the war in 2022.

recent_articles.title: US, Iran inch closer to deal to end the war: What to know | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **President Donald Trump** announced on Truth Social that a deal between the **United States**, **Iran**, and several other countries in the region has been largely negotiated, with details to be announced soon. The proposed memorandum of understanding (MoU) reportedly includes reopening the Strait of Hormuz, formally ending the US-Israel war on Iran, and opening a 30-day negotiation window for a broader peace agreement. **Iran** officials have confirmed negotiations are ongoing but pushed back against some of Trump's claims, emphasizing that major disagreements remain, particularly regarding the status of the Strait of Hormuz, Iran’s nuclear program, and conflicts involving Tehran-backed groups in Lebanon. The main sticking points include the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's nuclear program, and potential reparations for the conflict. While some analysts believe a deal is achievable, others highlight the need for Israel to acquiesce to ensure its success.

recent_articles.title: Former prosecutor calls for EU statute blocking US sanctions on ICC members | International criminal court | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A former **ICC** prosecutor, Fatou Bensouda, called for an EU-wide statute blocking US sanctions on the court's officials.  She argued that the sanctions are coercive attempts to interfere with the court's judicial functions and represent a misuse of international law. Bensouda criticized the lack of concrete action from states parties, including the Dutch government, which has signed an agreement to protect ICC personnel but has done little in practice to defend the court. She urged for "structural resistance" through legal mechanisms and financial safeguards for the court and its staff.  The US imposed sanctions on 11 **ICC** officials in response to the court's decision to issue arrest warrants for Israeli cabinet members, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

recent_articles.title: Iran Nuclear Deal: Iran agrees to give up enriched uranium as deal with Donald Trump 'largely negotiated': Report - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Iran** has agreed in principle to give up its stockpile of highly enriched uranium as part of a proposed agreement with the **United States**, according to The New York Times.  The deal, aimed at ending the ongoing conflict and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, would see Iran relinquish the uranium stockpile through negotiations later.  While President Donald Trump has described the deal as "largely negotiated", Iranian officials have maintained that nuclear issues are not currently part of the immediate discussions. The proposed agreement could include a formal declaration ending the war, reopening the Strait of Hormuz and launching fresh negotiations over Iran’s nuclear program lasting between 30 and 60 days.
